summary:
Observed facts. The #134 implementation is present and coherent in the frozen tree: scripts/duo-build.cjs (check/start/review/resume, pinned goal+task+reference hashes, per-round frozen tree+manifest+diff+request+invocation+prompt, read-only peer invocation, recursion guard, snapshot-drift rejection before and after review, initial review plus at most three repair rounds), skills/duo-build/SKILL.md, docs/duo-build.md, the bin/specflow.js `duo-build` entry (tree/bin/specflow.js:29-34) and 19 tests in tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js. manifest.json:1434/1498/1970 lists scripts/duo-build.cjs, skills/duo-build/SKILL.md and the test file although none appear in diff.patch and index.patch is empty, so untracked/uncommitted capture (REQ-04/AC-4) is directly demonstrated on this round. Direction matches the run goal and bounded objective: the builder stays interactive, the peer is read-only, and status()/docs/duo-build.md:61-63 both state acceptance never means merged or deployed (AC-6).

Prior findings against resolution evidence. F1 is resolved: tree/evidence/duo-build/full-tests.txt shows `npm test -- --runInBand`, exit 0, 41/41 suites and 921/921 tests passed with no skipped line (so zero skips repository-wide, including the duo-build suite), and tree/evidence/duo-build/contract-tests.txt shows `npm test -- contracts --runInBand`, exit 0, 27/27 suites, 626/626 passed. That satisfies tree/CLAUDE.md Rule 3 and Rule 4 for a change that adds scripts/*.cjs under PROJ-003 and a new CLI command. F2 is mostly resolved: check() now asserts a codex logged-in signal before returning (tree/scripts/duo-build.cjs:51-53), the fixed `permission` prose string is gone, replaced by `artifactAccess: 'not yet verified'` which is only upgraded to a peer-reported label after the review (duo-build.cjs:190), and the requested negative test exists and passes (tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js:97-103, asserting blocked, no peer record and exactly two provider calls). One part of F2 is not evidenced and is the single blocker below.

Live versus simulated. Confirmed live this round: my own invocation.json is `claude -p` with `--tools Read,Glob,Grep`, `--allowedTools Read,Glob,Grep`, `dontAsk`, `--safe-mode`, no write tool; check() ran before I was launched, so the claude auth path including the new combined stdout+stderr parse is live-exercised. Confirmed live earlier: tree/.specflow/duo/1789574648028-91fde804/proof/codex/stderr.txt is a genuine `codex exec` transcript (v0.154.0, sandbox read-only, approval never) in which Codex read the frozen files, independently reran the fixture and returned the structured accept recorded in proof/codex/review.json; the round-002 changes_required record with F1/F2 is durable at ../round-002/review.json with stdout.txt/stderr.txt alongside it, so AC-3/AC-5 flow of real peer output and findings is demonstrated. Simulated and labelled as such: all provider responses in the unit suite; the interactive Claude host in the codex-direction smoke (runner setting), which batch.json:3 and live-cycle.md:29-33 state honestly.

Status distinctions. Implemented and locally tested with full and contract suites green; two real peer reviews executed; nothing committed, merged, deployed, CI-run or customer-validated, and no PR/CI export is claimed or required by the batch. Hypothesis, not confirmed cause, for the blocker: the codex login-status regex may well match the real CLI, but no attached artifact shows it, and the only real codex run recorded the pre-fix peer shape, so it cannot support the post-fix gate. Acceptance would cover this batch scope only and would not imply any release gate.

peer.artifactAccess: peer reported required artifact inspection; see raw transcript

findings.basis: Unresolved remainder of prior finding F2, against REQ-03 ("Check installation/auth/permission. Peer unavailable means blocked, never verified") and AC-7 ("labelling simulations/unavailable capabilities accurately"). The fix replaces an unconditional `authenticated: true` with a gate coupled to an exact Codex CLI output string, and no attached evidence shows that gate has ever run against the real Codex CLI. Concrete material risk: if the string does not match the installed CLI's wording, every claude-code-builder run fails closed with "Codex authentication not confirmed by login status", making the entire reverse direction (half of REQ-07/AC-1) unusable for an authenticated user, while batch.json states the resolution as "Codex auth output checked explicitly".
findings.evidence: tree/scripts/duo-build.cjs:51-53 — `const auth = invoke(exe, exe === 'claude' ? ['auth','status'] : ['login','status'], { combineOutput: true }); ... if (exe === 'codex' && !/Logged in using\s+\S/i.test(auth)) throw Error('Codex authentication not confirmed by login status')`. The only support is a self-authored double: tree/tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js:15 returns the literal 'Logged in using ChatGPT', and the negative test at tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js:97-103 returns the literal 'Not logged in'. batch.json:28-36 cites only scripts/duo-build.cjs, tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js and evidence/duo-build/full-tests.txt for F2. A grep of the whole frozen tree for "Logged in|login status" returns only those code/test/doc lines — no raw `codex login status` output exists anywhere in the snapshot. tree/.specflow/duo/1789574648028-91fde804/proof/codex/review.json:6-11 records the only real Codex run with the pre-fix peer shape (`"permission": "checked by actual artifact inspection during review"`, a field the fix removed in favour of `artifactAccess`/`enforcedMode`), proving that smoke predates this change and cannot evidence it. tree/evidence/duo-build/live-cycle.md:35 ("Both provider CLIs were installed and authenticated") describes the pre-fix runs.
findings.action: In the same environment, run `codex login status` and `codex --version`, capture command line, raw combined output and exit code into a repository-relative file such as evidence/duo-build/codex-auth.txt, confirm that `/Logged in using\s+\S/i` matches that actual output (adjust the assertion to the real wording if it does not), and add the file to batch.evidence. Equivalent and stronger: re-run the reverse-direction smoke with the current helper so check() executes live and the round record shows the new `artifactAccess`/`enforcedMode` fields, then attach that record. Either way, state in evidence/duo-build/live-cycle.md whether the Codex readiness gate is live-verified or double-only, and re-review under the same `implementation` batch id.

unrelated: tree/evidence/duo-build/unit-tests.txt is stale: it lists 13 tests, but tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js now defines 19 (two parameterised repair tests, two parameterised installer tests, plus the new unauthenticated-codex, interrupted-attempt, resume-invalidation and executable-mode tests). tree/evidence/duo-build/live-cycle.md:7 likewise says "13 focused tests". Not blocking, since full-tests.txt supersedes it with zero skips, but the artifact should be refreshed or removed so it cannot be read as the current suite size.

check() hardcodes `enforcedMode` strings ('Read/Glob/Grep only, dontAsk' / 'read-only sandbox, approval never') at tree/scripts/duo-build.cjs:54 instead of deriving them from invocation(). They match today's flags (verifiable against this round's invocation.json), but a future flag change would leave the durable readiness record silently misstating the enforced mode. Deriving the label from the same invocation spec would keep the record self-consistent.

The customer-visible instruction `/duo-build #905` (README.md and tree/docs/duo-build.md:21) is still unverified as a Claude Code slash invocation; no .claude/commands/duo-build.md ships (manifest.json:2-9 lists only readme-audit and readme-restructure), and skills install to .claude/skills. The batch scope explicitly defers native interactive launch, so this is not blocking here, but it is a prominent published value that should be confirmed before release.

The new .gitignore rule `.specflow/duo/` means live-cycle.md's relative links to round-002/round-003 review records and the proof/ directory resolve only on the author's machine. The intent is stated ("Durable local duo-build snapshots and peer transcripts"), but the ticket's DoD "Live build/review/correction/re-review artifacts are readable" will need an explicit export, as was done for the two proof files force-included in this batch's evidence.

Snapshot capture still aborts the whole run on any symlink outside node_modules (tree/scripts/duo-build.cjs:23-34). A repository with a legitimately committed symlink can never be reviewed; recording symlinks as an explicit unsupported-entry list in snapshot-policy.json would degrade more gracefully.

Stale-lock recovery at tree/scripts/duo-build.cjs:134-138 rethrows any process.kill error whose code is not ESRCH, so a corrupt or non-numeric review.lock (NaN pid) leaves the run permanently unreviewable until the file is deleted by hand.

validateReview still only checks that requiredReads appear in the peer's self-reported `inspected` array (tree/scripts/duo-build.cjs:125-127); a peer can list paths it never opened. The derived label at line 190 now honestly says "peer reported", which is an improvement, but the underlying claim remains unverifiable from the helper's side.
tree/skills/README.md documents only specflow-loop-selector and does not mention the new duo-build skill, and templates/AGENTS.md work routing does not say which route duo-build belongs to.
